description_preview:
About Fractio
Professional services firms now deliver client work with two inputs: human judgment and AI. Their billing, cost, and project management systems were built for a one-input world where every hour is a human hour. So they can't see what AI actually cost to produce a deliverable, or what the human judgment behind it was worth.
Fractio makes both visible. Our patent-pending transaction infrastructure treats AI as a capital input distinct from human labor. It separately meters and attributes each input at the unit-of-work level, then routes every transaction through established economic and labor laws so the price reflects the true value of each input before payment releases.
Firms see their true cost of producing expertise for every deliverable, then roll it up across clients, teams, practice areas, and their entire book of business. With that view, they decide whether to keep, share, scale, or expand the margin AI creates.
Most tools look down at the hours, tasks, and tokens consumed. Fractio looks up at the outcome that was delivered and verified.
The Role
Demand from mid-market diagnostic and pilot professional services customers is growing, so we're adding two engineering interns ahead of it. You'll report directly to our Founder & CEO and work alongside our backend and frontend engineers. You'll own defined pieces of the platform that customers rely on to understand both what their AI costs and what their people's judgment is worth.
This is applied AI engineering at the infrastructure layer. You won't be training foundation models. You'll help make the value of human judgment and the cost of AI legible to a CFO, from a single deliverable up to the whole portfolio.
What You'll Work On
• AI usage and cost data: Extend how we capture usage and cost from AI models, tools, and agentic systems, and connect it to the client, workflow, and deliverable it served.
• Customer onboarding: Help classify the AI tools customers use and support the configuration each new customer needs as they onboard.
• Data quality: Help build checks that flag when usage can't be cleanly attributed to a unit of work, under messy conditions like shared API keys, overlapping usage, and incomplete data.
• Workflow integrations: Help connect delivery work in the tools firms already use (Jira, Asana, Linear, Notion, Monday) to Fractio, where outcomes are verified and settled.
• Anomaly detection: Prototype detection for unusual patterns that distort cost data across many deliverables.
• Portfolio analytics: Help build reporting that rolls unit-of-work results up to the client, team, practice, and book-of-business level, so firms can see where human judgment creates the most value.
What We're Looking For
Required:
• Currently enrolled in, or graduated within the past year from, a program in Computer Science, Data Science, Computer Engineering, Applied Math, or a related field
• Strong Python, including pandas/NumPy, REST APIs, and JSON
• Hands-on experience calling LLM APIs (OpenAI, Anthropic, or similar), and a working understanding of tokens, context windows, and model pricing
• Solid grounding in statistics: you can reason about confidence, error, and bias in a measurement, not just fit a model
• Comfortable in a fast-moving startup where you're expected to ask sharp questions
Nice to have:
• Experience with LLM gateways or observability tools (OpenRouter, LiteLLM, Helicone, Langfuse)
• Familiarity with MCP (Model Context Protocol) or agentic frameworks
• SQL and data modeling
• Exposure to Stripe, webhooks, or event-driven systems
• Interest in accounting, cost accounting, or the economics of professional services
• Coursework in anomaly detection or time-series analysis
What You'll Gain
• Production ownership of real components used by paying customers
• Direct mentorship from Fractio's founder, plus day-to-day collaboration with our engineering team
• A front-row seat to an early-stage startup: product, IP, go-to-market, and fundraising
• A portfolio at the intersection of AI engineering and financial infrastructure, a space very few engineers have worked in yet
• Hybrid Access to our office within the Embarc Collective startup community in Tampa
How to Apply
Interns sign a confidentiality and IP assignment agreement before starting, since the work involves proprietary methods and anonymized customer data.
Apply through LinkedIn and include:
• Your resume
• A link to your GitHub or a project you've built with an LLM API
• A short note (3–5 sentences) about a time you had to measure or track something when the data was messy, incomplete, or didn't quite answer the question you were asking. What did you do, and how did you know whether your result could be trusted?

October–December 2026 (about 10–12 weeks), 10–15 hours/week

Description
Amazon is seeking exceptional software engineering talent to develop the on-robot software components that connect intelligent robots to fleet-scale cloud systems, enabling telemetry collection, model deployment, over-the-air updates, and fleet coordination at unprecedented scale. We're building revolutionary software infrastructure that combines AI, large-scale distributed systems, and advanced robotics orchestration to create adaptable automation solutions capable of coordinating heterogeneous robot fleets safely alongside humans in dynamic industrial environments.
As a Software Development Engineer, you will own on-robot software components that bridge the gap between autonomous robot intelligence and cloud-based fleet management. You will work at the intersection of embedded systems and cloud-connected distributed architectures, ensuring that on-robot software operates reliably under real-time constraints, bandwidth limitations, and the safety requirements of industrial environments where robots work alongside humans. Your work will enable robots to receive fleet coordination commands, publish operational telemetry, receive over-the-air software and model updates, and participate as intelligent members of a coordinated fleet.
The ideal candidate brings deep expertise in software development with a strong understanding of how systems integrate with cloud infrastructure and large-scale distributed operations. You are hands-on, writing production-quality code and building resilient software that operates in resource-constrained environments. You can reason about latency requirements, failure modes, data flow direction, and graceful degradation. If you're passionate about building the software that makes robots smarter, more connected, and more capable as part of a coordinated fleet, this role offers the chance to make a lasting impact on the future of automation.
Key job responsibilities
Design, develop, and maintain on-robot software components that enable reliable connectivity between robots and cloud systems, supporting capabilities such as telemetry, remote updates, fleet coordination, and continuous learning.
Build software that operates reliably under real-time constraints, handling bandwidth-constrained environments, intermittent connectivity, and the sensor data volumes generated by modern industrial robots.
Collaborate with on-robot teams through joint architecture sessions to define and maintain clean software interfaces, with boundaries shaped by latency requirements, scope of optimization, data flow direction, failure modes, and development velocity.
Develop and maintain automated test frameworks for on-robot software components, including hardware-in-the-loop testing, simulated fleet scenarios, and integration tests that validate the on-robot to cloud communication path end to end.
Collaborate with applied science and data infrastructure teams to ensure on-robot telemetry and model deployment components meet the requirements of continuous learning pipelines and fleet intelligence systems.
Collaborate with fleet management and platform teams to ensure on-robot components integrate cleanly with fleet management software, platform services, deployment infrastructure, and monitoring and alerting systems.
Contribute to the design of robot communication APIs and platform architecture, ensuring they support scalability and multi-tenant requirements for both internal operations and future external customers.
Leverage AI-native development practices and AI coding assistants to accelerate development while maintaining the quality and reliability standards required for software systems in industrial environments.

3+ years of non-internship professional software development experience
2+ years of non-internship design or architecture (design patterns, reliability and scaling) of new and existing systems experience
1+ years of software development engineer or related occupational experience
1+ years of designing and developing large-scale, multi-tiered, multi-threaded, embedded or distributed software applications, tools, systems, and services using: C#, C++, Java, or Perl experience
1+ years of Object Oriented Design experience
Bachelor's degree or foreign equivalent in Computer Science, Engineering, Mathematics, or a related field
Experience programming with at least one software programming language

3+ years of full software development life cycle, including coding standards, code reviews, source control management, build processes, testing, and operations experience
Bachelor's degree in computer science or equivalent

Product Engineer — Regulatory AI Platforms
Engagement
: Part-time independent contractor — ~25–35 hours per week, flexible scheduling
Location

Term
: Initial 6-month engagement with a defined path to an expanded or full-time role as we scale
Compensation
: Hourly, commensurate with experience
About Us
LexReg is a regulatory intelligence platform for banks, credit unions, and fintechs. We offer the LexRegPulse and LexRegulator platforms. LexRegPulse monitors more than 130 federal and state regulatory and industry sources overnight and publishes a synthesized intelligence brief by 6:45 AM ET. Underneath the brief sits the thing that actually matters: a structured, versioned corpus of U.S. banking regulation, broken down into individual, separately citable obligations — the corpus that powers LexRegulator, our charter-scoped AI compliance agent.
Our product promise is that every claim we make traces to a real obligation, every obligation traces to a pinned primary source, and every source is being watched for change. Nothing is paraphrased. Nothing is asserted without a citation a customer can click. Only signal, no noise. This is the bleeding edge of legal and compliance utilization of Agentic AI and the future of the practice.
That promise is only as good as the systems that enforce it.
The Role
You will work with our team and help build products, end to end, across three areas:
Partner platforms
. Products that other companies’ engineers integrate against. You take these from a conversation with the business to production.
The corpus and the checks around it
. Collectors for sources that publish a PDF with no stable URL and no change notification. The schema and its versioning: supersession, amendments, effective dates, and applicability by charter type and asset threshold.
The tooling and the alarms
. The review console, and the per-source health, extraction-yield, and alerts.
How We Work
Agents propose, humans dispose. Automation drafts; it never commits. The commit moment is always a human click. Your job is to make that click well-informed, fast, and reversible —never to route around it.
Work arrives in a queue with a recommendation attached. If we are relying on anyone to remember to check something, we have built it wrong.
Fail loud, never fail quiet. Silent degradation is the only unacceptable outcome.
Deterministic beats probabilistic. If a check can be a string comparison, a schema constraint, or an HTTP status code, it is not an LLM judgment.
The same standard applies to our own code. We have shipped a quality bar no score could reach, and a verdict computed from a field that was never loaded. Both passed review. Finding that class of defect is the job, not an interruption to it.
Who You Are
We hire for the bar, not the résumé.
A current undergraduate or graduate student in engineering, computer science or a related field, or a recent graduate, able to commit 25–35 hours per week.
Working TypeScript and SQL, and a real project you can show — shipped, public, or from an internship or research — that ingests or parses data from a source that did not cooperate.
Or
Two or more years building data-intensive systems in production and keeping them honest. Fluent in TypeScript and SQL; comfortable in Postgres and Prisma. You have designed a schema you later had to migrate, and you have opinions about it now.
You have parsed hostile inputs: inconsistent HTML, PDFs with no text layer, tables that are images, and pagination that changes shape.
You have shipped something that works with an LLM, and you are appropriately skeptical of it. You have been burned by a model that was fluent and wrong; you built a check instead of a better prompt.
Required
Familiarity with AI platforms and using AI to enable efficient development.
You work alongside agentic coding tools and treat their output as a draft written in a confident voice. You can tell a plausible difference from a correct one. When the build is green, your instinct is to verify the claim against production rather than merge.
No ego about escalating.
Intellectual curiosity and honesty under commercial pressure. You will sometimes be the person saying a pipeline is not good enough to ship.
Helpful, Not Required
Bank or credit union compliance, examination, or supervisory correspondence.
Send a résumé to: Emanuel Slater at: emanuel@lexregpulse.com.
If you want to show us something — problem solving work you are proud of — feel free to share it, and tell us what broke and what you did about it.
LexRegPulse is an equal opportunity employer. We evaluate every applicant on the work.

At Amazon, we hire the best minds in technology to innovate on behalf of our customers. Security engineers use cutting-edge technology to solve complex problems and get to see the impact of their work first-hand.
The challenges security engineers solve for at Amazon are big and impact millions of customers, sellers, and products around the world. Our path is not always simple, so we are selective about who joins us on this journey. There is a certain kind of person who takes on this role at Amazon – someone who is excited by the idea of creating new products, features, and services from scratch while managing ambiguity and the pace of a company whose ship cycles are measured in weeks, not years.

As a Security Engineer, You Will/may
Collaborate with experienced Amazonians to create and execute security controls, defenses, and countermeasures to intercept and prevent internal and/or external attacks.

Work effectively with your team to identify security problems and improve the security aspects of their service(s).
Assess risks that could affect the confidentiality, integrity, or availability of data, systems, or services.

Classify, store, and handle data in accordance with policy or best practices.
Troubleshoot, research the root cause of, and resolve security or risk issues with guidance.
A day in the life
We’re on the lookout for the curious, those who think big and want to define the world of tomorrow.
At Amazon, you will grow into the high impact, visionary person you know you’re ready to be. Every day will be filled with exciting new challenges, developing new skills, and achieving personal growth.

Currently has, or is in the process of obtaining, a Bachelor's degree or above in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Information Technology or related fields

At LangChain, our mission is to make intelligent agents ubiquitous. We began as widely adopted open-source tools and have grown to also offer a platform for building, evaluating, deploying, and operating agents at scale.
With $125M raised at Series B from IVP, Sequoia, Benchmark, CapitalG, and Sapphire Ventures, we’re at a stage where we’re continuing to develop new products, growth is accelerating, and all team members have meaningful impact on what we build and how we work together. LangChain is a place where your contributions can shape how this technology shows up in the real world.
Today, our platform includes LangSmith (Observability, Evaluation, Deployment, Fleet, and Sandboxes), our open source frameworks (LangChain, LangGraph, and Deep Agents), and the newly launched LangSmith Engine for autonomous agent improvement. We have 100M+ monthly open source downloads, 6,000+ active LangSmith customers, and 5 of the Fortune 10 use LangSmith in production (+ 35% of the Fortune 500 overall), including teams at Klarna, Clay, Coinbase, Workday, Lyft, Cloudflare, Harvey, Rippling, Vanta, LinkedIn, Monday.com, Nvidia, and Bridgewater.

Develop new user-facing features using React & Typescript
Build reusable components and front-end libraries for future use
Translate designs and wireframes into high-quality code
Optimize components for maximum performance across a vast array of web-capable devices and browsers
Collaborate with fullstack and backend developers and UX/UI designers, to enhance usability

2+ years of Front-end engineering experience with strong proficiency in React, JavaScript and TypeScript
Hands-on experience with front-end development tools like Babel, Vite, Webpack, NPM, and Yarn
Familiarity with REST APIs and experience working closely with fullstack and backend engineers
Knowledge of modern authorization mechanisms, such as JWTs
A passion for user experience, design and building clean, engaging, and intuitive interfaces
Strong written and oral communication skills, with the ability to explain technical concepts clearly and concisely to both technical and non-technical stakeholders
The DNA to thrive in a start-up, fast-paced environment. Views unstructured environments as an opportunity to figure out the most impactful work and help define the future success of the company

Actively participate in agile planning and execution using established processes
